key_insight: A fair, standardized benchmark shows that only the newest Graph Foundation Models based on Prior-data Fitted Networks outperform strong tuned GNN baselines for node property prediction.
engineering_relevance: For real-world graph applications like fraud detection and recommendation, model choice should prioritize rigorously benchmarked accuracy and inference cost rather than relying on the GFM label alone.
method: Reevaluate 9 recent GFMs on node property prediction under a fairer comparison protocol.
Compare all GFMs against strong, well-tuned GNN baselines.
Assess predictive performance alongside inference cost.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a rigorous reevaluation of 9 GFMs and finds that only the most recent Prior-data Fitted Networks variants beat well-tuned GNNs, and only at higher inference cost.
watch_item: The better-performing GFM variants incur higher inference cost, so deployment may trade off latency and compute efficiency against accuracy.
paper_title: A Fair Evaluation of Graph Foundation Models for Node Property Prediction
